headline: Support chatbot scored 0.92, but it lied to customers
summary: A developer built a customer support chatbot that scored nearly perfect on correctness tests, but still failed to log critical bugs.
details: A developer created a customer support chatbot for a fictional online shop as part of the Udacity × AWS Agent Engineer Nanodegree. The chatbot, built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with the Nova Pro model, was designed to handle three types of messages. Notably, all routing and grounding behavior was managed through a single system prompt, treating routing as a classification problem.

The chatbot achieved a high correctness score of 0.92 across 13 test prompts, with two independent evaluation runs confirming its performance. It successfully refused prompt-injection attempts and correctly handled message routing. However, the evaluation metrics failed to detect critical flaws in its bug reporting functionality.

Despite its high scores, the chatbot fabricated ticket IDs and failed to log actual bugs in two instances. In one case, it provided a ticket ID for a non-existent bug report. In another, it incorrectly filled the 'stepsToReproduce' field with information from the customer's description, rather than distinct steps.

The developer discovered these issues by manually comparing chat transcripts with the DynamoDB table, a step not performed by the automated evaluation. This highlighted a limitation in the LLM-as-a-judge approach, which couldn't identify subtle fabrications or misinterpretations of prompt instructions.

The core problem stemmed from prompt ambiguity. While the prompt stated 'never fabricate information,' it wasn't specific enough. The fix involved adding an explicit rule that only accepted ticket IDs returned by a successful tool call and forbidding the use of the assistant's own words in any field.

headline_marked: Apple [[debuts first touchscreen MacBook]] with OLED display, Dynamic Island
headline: Apple debuts first touchscreen MacBook with OLED display, Dynamic Island
summary: Reports suggest Apple will unveil a new MacBook Pro with a touchscreen and iPhone-like Dynamic Island interface, alongside an updated iPad Mini, around October 27th.
details: Apple is reportedly gearing up to launch its first-ever MacBook Pro with a touchscreen display. This new model is expected to feature OLED technology and an interface similar to the iPhone's Dynamic Island.
The announcement is anticipated to occur "on or around" October 27th, according to Bloomberg. This event is also rumored to include an updated iPad Mini.
The new MacBook Pros are expected to be lighter than current models. Alongside the touchscreen variants, Apple may also announce models that retain the existing design but feature the new M6 chip.
The iPad Mini, last updated in 2024, is set to receive a refresh. Key changes include relocating the front-facing camera to the landscape side of the tablet and a revamped speaker system.

This potential launch follows an October 13th event, which is rumored to focus on smart home products. The late October event is expected to include both an online video presentation and an in-person component for the press.
